definition_zh: 某人；有人；重要人物
definition_en: a person who is not named or known, or an important person
core_image: 门口放着一把没人认领的雨伞
scene: 有人把伞忘在门口了。 Somebody left an umbrella at the door.
sceneCN: 这里 somebody 是「某人；有人」（第 1 个义项）；句意：有人把伞忘在门口了。

senses.title: An unnamed person
senses.definition: a person who is not named or not known
senses.definitionCN: 没有被指名或不认识的人
senses.example: Somebody left an umbrella at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 有人把伞忘在门口了。
senses.why: Some plus body names a person without giving a name.
senses.whyCN: some 加 body，指一个人却不给出名字。

senses.title: An important person
senses.definition: a person of importance or fame
senses.definitionCN: 有地位或名气的人
senses.example: After the award, she was somebody in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 获奖之后，她成了城里的名人。

senses.whyCN: 「是一个人」变成了「是一个重要的人」。

definition_zh: 吸引力；吸引人的事物（景点）；引力
definition_en: the power of something to interest or please people, a place or thing that draws visitors, or a force that pulls objects together
core_image: 游乐园里最高的那座塔，人群都朝它走过去
scene: 导游在车上指着窗外一片灯火，告诉大家下一个看点。 The old castle is the town's main attraction.
sceneCN: 这里 attraction 是「吸引人的地方、景点」（第 2 个义项）；句意是这座古堡是镇上最主要的景点。

senses.title: Pulling power
senses.definition: the quality that makes people feel interested or drawn to something
senses.definitionCN: 使人产生兴趣、被牵过去的那种性质
senses.example: The attraction of country life is its peace.
senses.exampleCN: 乡村生活的吸引力在于它的宁静。
senses.why: The noun names the force itself rather than the thing exerting it, so it can describe an abstract quality like peace or freedom.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指的是「力」本身，而不是发出这股力的东西，所以可以形容宁静、自由这类抽象特质。

senses.title: Place worth visiting
senses.definition: a place or thing that people visit because it is interesting
senses.definitionCN: 因为有趣而吸引人去参观的地方或事物
senses.example: The castle is the town's main attraction.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古堡是镇上最主要的景点。
senses.why: The abstract pull is turned into a countable object: whatever does the pulling can be counted as one attraction among many.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的「拉力」被具体化成可数的东西：凡是发出吸引力的，都能算作众多景点中的一个。

senses.title: Force between objects
senses.definition: a force that makes objects move toward each other
senses.definitionCN: 使物体相互靠近的力
senses.example: Gravity is the force of attraction between masses.
senses.exampleCN: 重力是物体之间相互吸引的力。
senses.why: Physics kept the oldest and most literal part of the word: bodies really do pull one another, with no interest or feeling involved.
senses.whyCN: 物理学保留了这个词最古老、最字面的部分：物体确实在互相拉，其中没有兴趣或情感。

intro.en: Attraction turns the act of drawing into a thing: the pull itself.

definition_zh: 出版；发表；公布；网络发布；刊登
definition_en: to make something public — first by announcing it, then by printing and selling it, and now by posting it online
core_image: 一扇原本关着的门被推开，屋里的话、文稿和消息一下子涌到街上，所有人都能听见看见
scene: 编辑指着屏幕安排今晚九点的上线时间。 We publish the story at nine tonight.
sceneCN: 这里 publish 是「网络发布」（第 4 个义项：在网站或平台上发布内容）；句意：我们九点把报道发到网上，然后在任何人发现之前更新它。画面里有新闻编辑室、时钟和一个亮着的窗口；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 出版；发表；公布；发布；刊登

collocations.zh: 不发表就出局（学术界习语）

senses.title: Bringing out a book
senses.titleCN: 出版：把一本书做出来卖掉
senses.definition: to prepare and issue a book, magazine, or other work for sale or distribution
senses.definitionCN: 制作并发行书籍、杂志或其他作品以供销售或分发
senses.example: The press will publish her novel next spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家出版社将在明年春天出版她的小说。
senses.why: From late 14c. the verb meant 'issue (a book, etc.) to the public, cause to be printed and offered for sale'. The printed object is the first thing the word learns to push out of doors.
senses.whyCN: 从 14 世纪后期起，这个动词意为“向公众发行（书等），使被印刷并供销售”。印刷品是这个词最早学会推出门外的东西。

senses.title: Putting research into print
senses.titleCN: 发表：让研究进入公共记录
senses.definition: to make an article, paper, or piece of writing available to the public, especially in a journal
senses.definitionCN: 使文章、论文或文字为公众可得，尤指在期刊上
senses.example: They published the results in a medical journal.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把结果发表在一份医学期刊上。
senses.why: The book-issuing sense narrows to the author's act: the journal issues, the author publishes. What counts is that the work enters the public record where others can cite it.
senses.whyCN: 出书义收窄为作者的行为：期刊发行，作者发表。关键在于作品进入公共记录，别人可以引用。

senses.title: Making information public
senses.titleCN: 公布：把消息放到所有人面前
senses.definition: to make information public, especially officially or in a formal statement
senses.definitionCN: 使信息为公众所知，尤指官方或以正式声明的方式
senses.example: The company published its annual figures yesterday.
senses.exampleCN: 公司昨天公布了年度数据。
senses.why: The original mid-14c. sense was 'make publicly known, reveal, divulge, announce'. No printing is needed: a spoken announcement can publish a piece of news.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪中的本义是“使公众知晓、揭露、泄露、宣布”。不需要印刷：一句口头宣布也能“公布”一条消息。

senses.title: Posting on the internet
senses.titleCN: 网络发布：按下那个按钮
senses.definition: to post content on a website, platform, or social media account
senses.definitionCN: 在网站、平台或社交媒体账号上发布内容
senses.example: She publishes a new video every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周五发布一个新视频。
senses.why: The printing sense transfers to screens: a platform 'publishes' what it makes visible to all. The button is the modern press — one click, and the private becomes public.
senses.whyCN: 印刷义转移到屏幕上：平台“出版”它所展示给所有人的内容。按钮就是现代的印刷机——一点，私下之物就公开了。

senses.title: Releasing an edition
senses.titleCN: 发行、发售：某一版被放出去
senses.definition: to release a particular edition or issue for sale or distribution
senses.definitionCN: 为销售或分发而发行某一版次或期次
senses.example: The dictionary was first published in 1895.
senses.exampleCN: 这部词典于 1895 年首次出版发行。
senses.why: Publishing is also a dated event: a first edition appears, sells out, is reprinted. The verb names the moment the edition leaves the warehouse.
senses.whyCN: 出版也是一个有日期的事件：初版出现、售罄、重印。这个动词命名版次离开仓库的那一刻。

senses.title: Spreading it abroad: the oldest sense
senses.titleCN: 公开传播：最早的那个意思
senses.definition: to spread something among people; to make it known widely (the original sense)
senses.definitionCN: 把某事在人群中传播；使广为人知（本义）
senses.example: The rumour was published across the town within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 这个谣言一天之内就传遍了全镇。
senses.why: Old French publier meant 'make public, spread abroad, communicate', from Latin publicare. Before print and before media, publishing was simply spreading the word.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 publier 意为“使公开、传播四方、传达”，来自拉丁语 publicare。在印刷与媒体之前，publishing 只是把话传开。

senses.title: Carrying it in the paper
senses.definition: to carry an article, letter, or notice in a newspaper or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 在报纸或杂志上刊登文章、来信或通知
senses.example: The paper published his letter on the front page.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸把他的信刊登在头版。
senses.why: The medium becomes the agent: a paper publishes what it prints. The author may have written it, but the newspaper performs the public act.
senses.whyCN: 媒体成了施动者：报纸刊登它所印的内容。作者也许写了它，但执行公开行为的是报纸。

senses.title: To expose and denounce (archaic)
senses.titleCN: 揭发、公开谴责：把某人推到众人眼前
senses.definition: to disgrace or denounce someone publicly (an archaic sense)
senses.definitionCN: 公开使某人蒙羞或谴责某人（古旧义）
senses.example: The pamphlet published him as a traitor.
senses.exampleCN: 那本小册子公开指认他为叛徒。
senses.why: Late 14c. also recorded 'to disgrace, put to shame; denounce publicly'. Making someone public could mean exposing him to shame — publication as punishment, not information.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪后期还记录有“使蒙羞、羞辱；公开谴责”。把一个人公开，可以意味着让他暴露在羞耻中——公开即惩罚，而非告知。

senses.title: To be someone's publisher
senses.titleCN: 为……出书：长期替一位作者出书
senses.definition: to be the publisher of a writer's work over time
senses.definitionCN: 长期作为某位作者作品的出版者
senses.example: This house has published him for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家出版社已经为他出书二十年了。
senses.why: The verb can name an ongoing relationship, not just a single act. A publisher 'publishes' an author the way a gallery represents an artist: repeatedly, as a standing commitment.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以命名一种持续关系，而不只是单次行为。出版社“出版”一位作者，就像画廊代理一位艺术家：反复地、作为长期承诺。

intro.en: Publish is from Latin publicare 'make public', through Old French publier. It starts as 'announce', gains 'print and sell' in the late 14c., and later picks up 'post online'. The whole history is one move: from private to public.
intro.cn: publish 来自拉丁语 publicare“使公开”，经古法语 publier 进入英语。它从“宣布”开始，在 14 世纪后期获得“印刷并销售”义，后来又有“网上发布”。整部历史就是一个动作：从私下到公开。

items.en: Publicare meant 'to make public', from publicus 'of the people'. Publicus was altered from Old Latin poplicus, from populus 'people'; the deeper origin of populus is uncertain and is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: publicare 意为“使公开”，来自 publicus“属于人民的”。publicus 由古拉丁语 poplicus 变来，后者来自 populus“人民”；populus 更深的来源不确定，标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Publier meant 'make public, spread abroad, communicate'. The French verb carries the word into English with the sense of spreading news among people.
items.cn: publier 意为“使公开、传播四方、传达”。这个法语动词带着“在人群中传播消息”的意思进入英语。

items.en: Publicen appears in English with the sense 'make public'. It is the direct borrowing of the French verb.
items.cn: publicen 以“使公开”之义出现在英语中，是对法语动词的直接借用。

items.en: Publishen is an alteration of publicen, probably by influence of banish and finish. It means 'make publicly known, reveal, divulge, announce'.
items.cn: publishen 是 publicen 的变体，可能受 banish、finish 等词影响。它意为“使公众知晓、揭露、泄露、宣布”。

items.en: The printing sense appears: 'issue (a book, etc.) to the public, cause to be printed and offered for sale'. The same period records 'to disgrace, put to shame; denounce publicly', and the odd sense 'to people, populate; to multiply'.
items.cn: 印刷义出现：“向公众发行（书等），使被印刷并供销售”。同一时期还记录有“使蒙羞、羞辱；公开谴责”，以及奇怪的“使人居住、繁殖”义。

items.en: Publishing becomes an industry with publishers, editions and copyright; in the late 20c. the verb extends to websites and social platforms, where 'publish' means 'make visible to everyone'.
items.cn: 出版在 19 至 20 世纪成为拥有出版商、版次与版权的产业；20 世纪后期，这个动词扩展到网站与社交平台，publish 意为“让所有人看见”。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the publ- or -ish shape but not the sense; the near group names the various acts of releasing words to the world.
note.cn: 形近组共享 publ- 或 -ish 的外形，但意义不同；近义组命名把文字释放给世界的各种动作。

entries.definition: open to all; of the people. It is the adjective behind publish, but has no verb ending.

entries.definition: to make someone suffer for a wrong. It rhymes with publish but comes from a different root.

entries.definition: to make something smooth and shiny. It differs from publish by a single vowel.

entries.definition: fit to be published. It is the same verb plus the suffix -able.
entries.definitionCN: 可出版的。它是同一个动词加上后缀 -able。

entries.definition: to reproduce text or images on paper. It is the physical half of publishing.
entries.definitionCN: 在纸上复制文字或图像。它是出版的物质一半。

entries.definition: to release something officially, such as stamps, shares, or an edition.
entries.definitionCN: 正式发行某物，如邮票、股票或一个版次。

entries.definition: to make a film, record, or statement available to the public.

entries.definition: to tell people about something officially. It matches publish in the 'make public' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 正式告知人们某事。它对应 publish 的“使公开”义。

entries.definition: to pass something from person to person or place to place.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物在人与人、地与时之间流传。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin publicare 'make public', Old French publier, and the modern publisher who turns a manuscript into a public object.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 publicare“使公开”、古法语 publier，以及把稿子变成公共物品的现代 publisher。

normal.en: publish = public + -ish: to make public, with a verb ending.
normal.cn: publish = public + -ish：使公开，只是多了一个动词词尾。

normal.en: The pair gives two nouns: publication (the act or thing) and publicity (the attention).
normal.cn: 这一对给出两个名词：publication（行为或物品）与 publicity（注意力）。

normal.en: A publisher is the person who pushes the door open; publishing is the industry built around that push.
normal.cn: publisher 是推开门的人；publishing 是围绕这一推建立的产业。

normal.en: 'Publish or perish' is the academic rule: if your work is not made public, it does not count.
normal.cn: “publish or perish（不发表就出局）”是学术规则：作品若未公开，就不算数。

normal.en: Press 'Publish' on a blog and the old printing metaphor happens instantly.
normal.cn: 在博客上按下“发布”，那个古老的印刷隐喻瞬间发生。

abstract.en: The core is a door: what was inside is now outside, available to anyone.
abstract.cn: 核心是一扇门：原本在里面的，现在到了外面，任何人都能得到。

abstract.en: The word moves through three machines: voice, press, network — the same act each time.
abstract.cn: 这个词穿过三台机器：嗓音、印刷机、网络——每次都是同一个动作。

abstract.en: Publish can inform or expose; the same opening of a door can be a gift or a punishment.
abstract.cn: publish 可以是告知，也可以是揭发；同一扇门的打开，可以是礼物，也可以是惩罚。

examples.en: The journal publishes articles on climate policy every month.
examples.cn: 这份期刊每月发表气候政策方面的文章。

examples.en: The government published the new safety rules on its website.
examples.cn: 政府在网站上公布了新的安全规则。

examples.en: He published his first photograph at the age of sixteen.
examples.cn: 他十六岁时发表了自己的第一张照片。

dict_mnemonic.text: public（公众）+ ish（动词）——把东西放到公众面前；谐音“帕布利什”：把稿子“扑”进印刷机，立刻（lish）公开 → publish 出版；发表

root: 源自拉丁语 publicare“使公开”，由 publicus“属于人民的”构成，经古法语 publier 进入英语；核心是“把原本关在屋里的东西推给所有人”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, one movement outward. A voice announces, a press prints and sells, a journal carries research, a company releases figures, a website posts a video, and an old sense even exposes a person to public shame.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项，一个向外的动作。嗓音宣布，印刷机印出并销售，期刊承载研究，公司发布数据，网站上传视频，还有一个古老义把一个人推到公众的羞耻里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed door opened — words, writing, or news released to everyone at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇关着的门被打开——话语、文字或消息一下子释放给所有人。

branches.en: THE PRINTED OBJECT: bringing out a book, and releasing a particular edition.
branches.cn: 印刷品：把一本书做出来，以及发行某个版次。

branches.en: THE MEDIUM: research published in a journal, and a letter carried by a newspaper.
branches.cn: 媒介：在期刊上发表研究，以及报纸刊登一封来信。

branches.en: MAKING KNOWN: official disclosure, and the oldest sense of spreading news abroad.
branches.cn: 使人知晓：官方公布，以及最古老的“传播四方”义。

branches.en: THE NETWORK: posting content where everyone can see it.
branches.cn: 网络：把内容发布到人人可见之处。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC GAZE: archaic public denunciation, and the publisher's long relation to an author.
branches.cn: 公众目光：古旧的公开谴责，以及出版者与作者的长期关系。

intro.en: Publish is publ- plus -ish. Its family shows Latin publicus 'of the people', the verb publicare, and the endings -er, -ing, -ation, -able and the negative prefix un-.
intro.cn: publish 是 publ- 加 -ish。它的词族展示拉丁语 publicus“属于人民的”、动词 publicare，以及词尾 -er、-ing、-ation、-able 和否定前缀 un-。

latinIntro.en: Latin publicare 'make public' yields publish and publication; publicus 'of the people' gives public, publicity and publicize, while un- and re- build unpublished and republish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 publicare“使公开”给出 publish 与 publication；publicus“属于人民的”给出 public、publicity、publicize，而 un- 与 re- 构成 unpublished 与 republish。

items.meaning: to make public; to issue a work
items.example: They publish a new edition every two years.
items.exampleCN: 他们每两年出版一个新版。

items.meaning: one who issues books or other works
items.example: Her publisher sent her the first proofs.
items.exampleCN: 她的出版商把初校样寄给了她。

items.meaning: the act or industry of issuing works
items.exampleCN: 数字出版改变了这个行业。

items.meaning: the act of publishing; a published work
items.example: The publication was delayed by a month.
The notes are interesting but not publishable.
items.exampleCN: 这些笔记有趣，但不适合发表。

items.meaning: not yet made public in print
items.example: The archive holds hundreds of unpublished letters.
items.exampleCN: 档案馆藏有数百封未发表的信件。
这篇文章于 1990 年重新发表。

items.example: The square is open to the public.
They publicized the concert across campus.
items.exampleCN: 他们在全校宣传了这场音乐会。

items.meaning: public attention; the state of being known
items.exampleCN: 这个案子引起了全国关注。

definition_zh: 网；蜘蛛网；网络；（鸭、蛙的）蹼
definition_en: a net of fine threads spun by a spider, and also any network of connected parts, especially the internet
core_image: 清晨的蛛丝挂在枝叶之间，露珠一颗颗停在每个交点上
scene: 天亮后小路上挂着许多蛛网，露水停在丝的交点上，走过去时前额碰到一片凉。 A web stretched across the path, strung with drops of dew.
sceneCN: 这里 web 是「蜘蛛网」（第 1 个义项：细丝结成的网络）；句意为一道蛛网横在小路上，挂着露水。挂在枝叶间、交点缀着露珠的蛛丝就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The net a spider spins
senses.definition: a fine net of threads spun by a spider to catch insects
senses.definitionCN: 蜘蛛吐丝结成的细网，用来捕捉昆虫
senses.example: A fly was caught in the web above the window.
senses.exampleCN: 一只苍蝇粘在窗上的蛛网里。
senses.why: This is the original sense: an animal-made net of threads.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：动物用丝结成的网。

senses.title: Any net of threads or straps
senses.definition: a woven or tied net, such as one used for carrying loads
senses.definitionCN: 用手工编结的网，如用来装运东西的网袋
senses.example: They carried the fruit home in a web of cord.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用绳网把水果扛回家。
senses.why: The same crossing structure is named for human-made nets.
senses.whyCN: 同样交错的结构，也用于人造的网。

senses.title: A network of connected things
senses.definition: a complex set of connected parts, people or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 由互相连接的部分、人或想法构成的复杂整体
senses.example: A web of canals links the villages.
senses.exampleCN: 纵横的运河把各村落连成一体。
senses.why: Lines meeting at many points look like a spider’s work at map scale.
senses.whyCN: 在许多点上相交的线，放大到地图尺度就像蜘蛛的作品。

senses.title: The internet
senses.definition: the system of linked pages and services accessed through the internet
senses.definitionCN: 通过互联网访问的相互链接的页面与服务的总称
senses.example: Our school put the timetable on the web.
senses.exampleCN: 我们学校把课程表放到了网上。
senses.why: Pages linked to pages repeat the spider’s image in electronic form.
senses.whyCN: 页面与页面相连，把蜘蛛的意象搬到电子世界里。

senses.title: The skin between toes
senses.definition: the skin joining the toes of a duck, frog or otter
senses.definitionCN: 鸭、蛙或水獭脚趾之间相连的皮
senses.example: The duck’s webbed feet pushed against the water.
senses.exampleCN: 鸭子的蹼在水里一推。
senses.why: The skin is a natural net, and English used its oldest net word for it.
senses.whyCN: 这层皮是天生的网，英语就用最古老的网词来称它。

senses.title: A weight or roll of paper
senses.definition: a large roll or sheet of paper made in one continuous piece
senses.definitionCN: 一次性制成的大卷或整幅纸张
senses.example: The press takes paper from a single web.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷机从一整卷纸中取纸。
senses.why: A continuous sheet of paper is spun and joined like a fabric, so printers call it a web.
senses.whyCN: 连续不断的纸幅像织物一样连成一片，印刷业便称之为 web。

intro.en: Web goes back to Old English webb, a word for woven cloth, which is also why the skin between a duck’s toes is called a web.
intro.cn: web 可上溯到古英语 webb，意为织成的布，这也正是鸭趾间那张皮被称为 web 的原因。

items.en: The Germanic root is the same one as weave, meaning a woven thing.
items.cn: 这一日耳曼词根与 weave 相同，指一件织成的东西。

items.en: Webb meant a piece of woven cloth and, by extension, any woven net.
items.cn: webb 指一块织成的布，引申为任何织成的网。

items.en: The spider sense became dominant because spider’s web was the everyday example.
items.cn: 蜘蛛义成为主流，因为蛛网是日常最常见的例子。

items.en: Web kept widening to canals, lies and other entangled structures.
items.cn: web 不断扩宽，用于运河、谎言等纠缠的结构。

items.en: In 1989 the World Wide Web gave the word its biggest modern extension.
items.cn: 1989 年万维网给了这个词最大的现代扩展。

note.en: The first group are web compounds of the computer age, the second the nets and tangles it resembles.
note.cn: 第一组是计算机时代的 web 复合词，第二组是它所比拟的网与纠缠。

entries.definition: One page of a website.

entries.definition: Strong woven strips used in straps.
entries.definitionCN: 带子；网状织物

entries.definition: A confused mass of threads or things.

normalIntro.en: Start with dew on a spider’s threads, then let the threads stretch to canals and to the internet.
normalIntro.cn: 从蛛丝上的露水开始，再让丝线延伸到运河与互联网。

normal.en: A spider’s web is made of threads the spider spins itself.
normal.cn: 蜘蛛网是蜘蛛自己吐丝结的。

normal.en: The Web with a capital letter is the internet system.
normal.cn: 大写的 Web 指万维网。

normal.en: Webbed feet are feet with skin between the toes.
normal.cn: webbed feet 是趾间有皮相连的脚。

normal.en: A web of lies is a set of lies all holding each other up.
normal.cn: a web of lies 是一张互相支撑的谎言网。

normal.en: A web of paper is one continuous width from the mill.
normal.cn: 纸的 web 是从造纸机出来的一整幅。

abstract.en: Picture a thread with one drop on each joint.
abstract.cn: 想一根丝、每个交点上一滴水珠。

abstract.en: Feel the cool line across your forehead.
abstract.cn: 感受额头上那一道凉丝。

abstract.en: See the same shape drawn over a map as roads.
abstract.cn: 看同样的形状被画在地图上成为道路。

examples.en: The garden was full of webs after the wet night.
examples.cn: 潮湿的夜里过后，花园里到处是蛛网。

examples.en: She typed the address into the web browser.
examples.cn: 她把地址输进网页浏览器。

examples.en: The old city is a web of narrow lanes.
examples.cn: 老城是一片纵横的窄巷网。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「韦布」——韦布老先生清早出门，一头撞进挂满露水的蛛网。

root: 日耳曼语编织词根 → 古英语 webb（织成的织物、网）→ 中古英语 web；同源词有 weave、webbed。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as woven cloth and thread, then net, then any connected structure, ending with the internet and even a roll of paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从织成的布与线出发，到网，再到任何互相连接的结构，最后到互联网甚至整卷纸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spider’s web strung with dew.
core.cn: 核心意象：挂着露水的蛛网。

branches.en: The spider branch: a fly caught above the window.
branches.cn: 蜘蛛分支：粘在窗上的苍蝇。

branches.en: The craft branch: a cord net for fruit.
branches.cn: 手工分支：装水果的绳网。

branches.en: The network branch: canals linking villages and pages linking pages.
branches.cn: 网络分支：连通村落的运河与互相链接的页面。

branches.en: The bodily and paper branch: webbed feet and a roll of paper.
branches.cn: 身体与纸张分支：蹼足与整卷纸。

branches.en: The origin branch: a spider spinning above the window.
branches.cn: 起源分支：在窗上结网的蜘蛛。

intro.en: Web compounds very freely in modern English, above all in computing.
intro.cn: web 在现代英语中极能复合，尤其在计算机领域。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; the Latin table is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，故拉丁表留空。

definition_zh: 陌生人；外人；外地人；不熟悉某事的人
definition_en: a person you do not know, a person from another place, or someone not used to something
core_image: 一个站在门口、你叫不出名字的人
scene: 一个陌生人敲了敲门。 A stranger knocked at the door.
sceneCN: 这里 stranger 是「陌生人」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一个陌生人敲了敲门。

senses.title: An unknown person
senses.definition: a person you do not know
senses.definitionCN: 你不认识的人
senses.example: A stranger knocked at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 一个陌生人敲了敲门。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of an unknown person.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示不认识的人的基本义项。

senses.title: An outsider
senses.definition: a person from another place or group
senses.definitionCN: 来自别处或别的群体的人
senses.example: They treat newcomers as strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把新来的人当外人。
senses.why: Someone from outside becomes a stranger.
senses.whyCN: 从外面来的人，就成了陌生人。

senses.title: Not used to something
senses.definition: a person who is not familiar with something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事不熟悉的人
senses.example: I am a stranger to this city.
senses.exampleCN: 我对这座城市很陌生。
senses.why: Being new to a thing is being a stranger to it.
senses.whyCN: 对某事陌生，就是它的陌生人。

definition_zh: 变化；变动；差异；变体、变奏；变异
definition_en: a change in amount, level or form, or a different version of something
core_image: 同一首歌被唱了五遍，每一遍的音高都略有不同
scene: 气象站的记录本上，同一个月的降雨量每年都不一样。 There is a wide variation in temperature between day and night in the desert.
sceneCN: 这里 variation 是「差异、变化幅度」（第 2 个义项：程度上的不同）；句意为沙漠里昼夜温差很大。同一首歌每遍音高略异，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：变化、变动、差异；变体、变奏；变异

collocations.zh: 主题变奏、略加改动的版本

senses.title: The act of changing
senses.titleCN: 变化：某物在改变的过程
senses.definition: the act or process of changing
senses.definitionCN: 正在改变的动作或过程
senses.example: Careful measurement showed a slight variation in pressure overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细测量显示夜间气压有细微变化。
senses.why: Latin variare means to change, and -atio names the act; the word is the process itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 variare 意为改变，-atio 命名这一行为；这个词就是过程本身。

senses.title: A difference in amount
senses.definition: a difference in amount, level or degree between things
senses.definitionCN: 事物之间在数量、水平或程度上的不同
senses.example: There is a wide variation in temperature between day and night in the desert.
senses.exampleCN: 沙漠里昼夜温差很大。
senses.why: Once difference is measured, the word shifts from process to size: the amount of difference.
senses.whyCN: 差异一旦被测量，这个词就从过程变成幅度：差了多少。

senses.title: A changed version
senses.definition: a thing that differs slightly from another of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 与同类事物略有不同的版本
senses.example: The chef offered a vegetarian variation of the same dish.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师给同一道菜提供了素食版本。
senses.why: The same base appears in a new shape; the family resemblance stays visible.
senses.whyCN: 同一个底子换了一个形状出现，家族的相似仍然看得见。

senses.title: A musical form
senses.titleCN: 变奏：把一个主题反复改写
senses.definition: a repeated melody altered in rhythm, key or harmony
senses.definitionCN: 把一段旋律在节奏、调性或和声上反复改写
senses.example: The pianist played a set of variations on a folk tune.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴家演奏了一组民谣主题变奏。
senses.why: Music makes the idea audible: one theme, many dresses.
senses.whyCN: 音乐让这个概念可以被听见：同一个主题，换很多件衣服。

senses.title: Biological difference
senses.titleCN: 变异：同种生物个体间的差别
senses.definition: differences between individuals of the same species, often inherited
senses.definitionCN: 同种生物个体之间的差别，常由遗传造成
senses.example: Genetic variation is what allows a population to adapt.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传变异使得一个种群能够适应环境。
senses.why: Living things copy themselves imperfectly, so each generation carries small differences that selection can use.
senses.whyCN: 生物复制自身时并不完美，于是每一代都带着细微差别，供自然选择使用。

intro.en: Variation is the Latin verb variare plus the noun ending -atio, a way of naming a process.
intro.cn: variation 是拉丁动词 variare 加名词词尾 -atio，用来给一个过程命名。

items.en: The verb variare meant to make different or to shift between forms.
items.cn: 动词 variare 意为使不同，或在各形式之间变换。

items.en: The noun variatio named the act of changing, with the ending -atio for an action.
items.cn: 名词 variatio 指改变的行为，词尾 -atio 表示动作。

items.en: Old French passed on variacion, still meaning a change or difference.
items.cn: 古法语传下 variacion，仍指变化或差异。

items.en: English took variation in the fourteenth century for changes in weather, price and form.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 variation，用于天气、价格与形式的变化。

items.en: Modern usage adds music and biology, giving the word a technical life beside its everyday one.
items.cn: 现代用法增添了音乐与生物学，使这个词在日常生活之外又有了术语的生命。

note.en: The look-alike group is the vari- family; the near-meaning group gathers words for difference and change.
note.cn: 形近组是 vari- 家族；近义组收表示差异与变化的词。

entries.definition: The verb, to differ or change by degrees.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「变化、不同」，是它的动词形式。

entries.definition: A form that differs from the standard one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变体」，与标准形式不同。

entries.definition: A range of kinds, rather than one change.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性、种类」，不是单次变化。

entries.definition: Something that is able to change.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」。

entries.definition: The plain noun for becoming different.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变化」，最普通的说法。

entries.definition: Rising and falling again and again, like a level.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「波动」，反复起落。

entries.definition: The gap between two things, without motion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「差别」，不含运动感。

entries.definition: One form of something that exists in several forms.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「版本」，几个形式中的一个。

normalIntro.en: The hooks lean on the vari- family and on phrases like variation on a theme.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子依靠 vari- 词族与 variation on a theme 这类搭配。

normal.en: Vary is the verb, variation is the change itself.
normal.cn: vary 是动词，variation 是变化本身。

normal.en: A variation on a theme is the same tune in new clothes.
normal.cn: variation on a theme 就是同一段旋律换了衣服。

normal.en: Genetic variation is why siblings are not identical.
normal.cn: 遗传变异是兄弟姐妹不完全相同的原因。

normal.en: Seasonal variation explains why prices move with the calendar.
normal.cn: 季节变化解释了价格为何跟着日历走。

normal.en: A wide variation means the numbers are far apart.
normal.cn: wide variation 指数字彼此差距很大。

abstract.en: Variation is difference with a memory: it tells you what the same thing looks like elsewhere.
abstract.cn: 变化是一种带记忆的差别：它告诉你同一事物在别处长什么样。

abstract.en: One process, several versions, many notes: the word carries all three without changing shape.
abstract.cn: 一个过程、几个版本、许多音符：这个词不变形就能承载三者。

abstract.en: Without variation there is no selection; difference is what time can work on.
abstract.cn: 没有差异就没有选择；时间能作用的正是差别。

examples.en: There is a wide variation in rainfall across the region.
examples.cn: 这个地区的降雨量差异很大。

examples.en: The design is a variation on a chair she made last year.
examples.cn: 这个设计是她去年做的一把椅子的变体。

examples.en: Small variations in temperature can change the result.
examples.cn: 温度的细微变化就可能改变结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威瑞一起」——威（风）瑞（雨）一起变，变化就来了：变化

root: 源自拉丁语动词 variare「改变」的名词形式 variatio，经古法语进入英语；同族词有 vary、variant、variety、variable。

sensesIntro.en: Variation covers a process, a measured gap, a new version, a piece of music and a fact of biology.
sensesIntro.cn: variation 涵盖一个过程、一个测得的差距、一个新版本、一段音乐和一条生物学事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same tune sung five times, each time a little different.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一首歌被唱了五遍，每遍都略有不同。

branches.en: PROCESS LINE: change happening over time.
branches.cn: 过程线：随时间发生的变化。

branches.en: SIZE LINE: how far the values sit apart.
branches.cn: 幅度线：数值之间差多少。

branches.en: FORM LINE: the same thing in a new dress.
branches.cn: 形式线：同一样东西换的新装。

branches.en: LIFE LINE: inherited differences in a species.
branches.cn: 生命线：种群中可遗传的差别。

branches.en: CONTRAST: variation is measured, difference is simply noticed.
branches.cn: 对照线：variation 要被测量，difference 只需被察觉。

intro.en: Variation is a root plus an action-noun ending; the whole vari- family shares that stem.
intro.cn: variation 是词根加表动作的名词词尾，整个 vari- 家族共用这个词干。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are variare, to change, and -atio, the action noun ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁构件是 variare「改变」和表示动作名词的 -atio。

items.example: It shows the word in use.

definition_zh: 残余；遗迹；遗体；剩余物
definition_en: the parts that are left after the rest has been used, destroyed, or taken away
core_image: 沙土里露出半截石墙，房屋本身早已不见
scene: 考古队在麦田下面挖出了几段石墙和一批陶片。 Under the wheat field, the team found the remains of a small Roman house.
sceneCN: 这里 remains 是「遗迹」（第 1 个义项：古代建筑残留的部分）；句意：在麦田下面，考古队发现了一座小罗马房屋的遗迹。

derivatives.zh: remains 的动词来源，义为「停留；剩下」
由同一「剩余」概念发展而来，义为「残余；零头」

senses.title: What is left after destruction
senses.definition: the parts of a building, object, or settlement that survive after the rest has gone
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、器物或聚落在其余部分消失后仍然存在的部分
senses.example: The remains of the city wall can still be seen.
senses.exampleCN: 城墙的残迹仍依稀可见。
senses.why: Remains is simply the plural of the verb used as a noun, so it names whatever has stayed behind while the rest went.
senses.whyCN: remains 就是动词的复数形式被用作名词，指其余部分消失后仍然留下来的东西。

senses.title: The body of a dead person
senses.definition: the body of a dead person or animal, used with care and formality
senses.definitionCN: 死者或死动物的身体，用于谨慎、正式的场合
senses.example: The remains were returned to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 遗骸被交还给了家属。
senses.why: What is left of a person after death is treated with the same respectful word used for ruins.
senses.whyCN: 人死之后所留下的部分，也用这个对待遗迹般的敬重字眼。

senses.title: Leftover food or material
senses.definition: the food or material that was not finished or used
senses.definitionCN: 没有吃完或用完的食物或材料
senses.example: She packed the remains of the cake into a box.
senses.exampleCN: 她把剩下的蛋糕装进了盒子。
senses.why: The everyday sense is the most literal: whatever is left on the table or in the workshop.
senses.whyCN: 最日常的义项最字面：桌上或作坊里没被用掉的那一部分。

intro.en: Remains is the plural of remain used as a noun; the noun developed in English rather than in Latin.
intro.cn: remains 是动词 remain 的复数形式被用作名词，这一名词用法在英语中发展而成，而非直接来自拉丁语。

items.en: Remanere, to stay behind, supplies the verb that the noun is built on.
items.cn: remanere「留在后面」提供了这个名词所依附的动词。

items.en: Old French remaindre gives English the verb remain.
items.cn: 古法语 remaindre 给英语带来了动词 remain。

items.en: The plural remains is used for what is left of a building or a meal.
items.cn: 十五世纪起，复数 remains 用来指建筑或饭菜剩下的部分。

items.en: The word becomes a formal and respectful term for the bodies of the dead.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，这个词成为指称死者遗体的正式而敬重的说法。

items.en: Archaeology fixes the sense of ancient remains, and the word stays plural in all uses.
items.cn: 考古学固定了「古代遗迹」这一义项，而这个词在各类用法中都保持复数。

note.en: Remains is a plural-only noun, and it stands beside words for ruins, relics, and leftovers.
note.cn: remains 是只用复数的名词，与表示废墟、遗物与残羹的词相邻。

entries.definition: to stay behind or continue to exist
entries.definitionCN: 停留；剩下，是 remains 的动词来源

entries.definition: still there after the rest has gone
entries.definitionCN: 剩余的，是同一词根的形容词形式

entries.definition: a small part left after the rest is gone
entries.definitionCN: 残余；零头，与 remains 意义接近但拼写不同

entries.definition: the broken parts of an old building
entries.definitionCN: 废墟；遗址，侧重破败状态

entries.definition: an object surviving from an earlier time
entries.definitionCN: 遗物；文物，强调有保存价值

entries.definition: food not eaten at a meal
entries.definitionCN: 剩饭；剩余食物，口语常用

normalIntro.en: Remains is the plural of remain, so the hooks all come back to things that stayed behind.
normalIntro.cn: remains 就是 remain 的复数，所以记忆钩子都回到「留下来的东西」。

normal.en: Treat it as a plural noun: the remains of a temple, the remains of a meal.
normal.cn: 把它当复数名词用：寺庙的遗迹、一餐的剩余。

normal.en: Human remains is the respectful phrase in news reports and official writing.
normal.cn: human remains 是新闻报道与官方文书中的敬重说法。

normal.en: Remains never takes a singular form in these senses, so avoid writing a remain.
normal.cn: 这些义项下 remains 没有单数形式，不要写成 a remain。

normal.en: The verb remain is the base, and the noun adds only an s.
normal.cn: 动词 remain 是基础，名词只加了一个 s。

normal.en: Archaeology reports often begin with the remains of a settlement.
normal.cn: 考古报告常常以某处聚落的遗迹开头。

abstract.en: Picture a broken wall sticking out of a field, the house long gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一段断墙从田里露出来，房子早已不在。

abstract.en: See a few crumbs and an empty plate after a birthday cake.
abstract.cn: 想象生日蛋糕之后留下的一点碎屑和空盘子。

abstract.en: Think of bones carefully laid in a wooden box.
abstract.cn: 想木盒里被小心安放的骸骨。

examples.en: The remains of the meal were given to the dog.
examples.cn: 剩下的饭菜给了狗。

examples.en: Workers uncovered human remains at the building site.
examples.cn: 工人在工地发现了人类遗骸。

examples.en: The museum displays remains from the Bronze Age.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出青铜时代的遗物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞梅子」——梅花落了，枝头还剩几颗梅子；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 动词 remain 的复数名词化，源自拉丁语 remanere（re-「留在后面」+ manere「停留」）。

sensesIntro.en: One plural noun covers ruins, corpses, and leftovers, because all three are what stayed after the rest went.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个复数名词涵盖遗迹、遗体与剩饭，因为三者都是其余部分消失后留下来的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a half-buried wall where a house once stood.
core.cn: 核心意象：房屋早已消失，只剩半埋在土里的石墙。

branches.en: Stone that outlasts its building is the archaeological sense.
branches.cn: 比建筑更长寿的石头，就是考古意义上的遗迹。

branches.en: What outlasts a person is named with the same respectful word.
branches.cn: 比人更长久留存的部分，也用同一个敬重的词来命名。

branches.en: What outlasts a meal is the plainest everyday leftover.
branches.cn: 比一餐饭更长久留存的，就是最日常的剩饭。

branches.en: Both ruins and human remains call for careful, formal language.
branches.cn: 遗迹与遗体都需要谨慎、正式的表达。

branches.en: Both are simply what the rest of the world left behind.
branches.cn: 两者都只是其余世界留下的那部分。

intro.en: Remains has no prefix of its own beyond the verb it comes from, but its Latin root is still clear.
intro.cn: remains 除所依附的动词外没有独立前缀，但其拉丁词根仍然清楚。

latinIntro.en: The chain runs from Latin manere, to stay, through remanere, to stay behind, to the English verb remain.
latinIntro.cn: 这条链从拉丁语 manere「停留」经 remanere「留在后面」到英语动词 remain。

items.example: The man- root also appears in mansion.
items.exampleCN: man- 词根也出现在 mansion 中。

items.example: Manere is the oldest layer of the family.
items.exampleCN: manere 是这个词族最古老的一层。

items.example: Re- adds the idea of staying behind.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 增添了「留在后面」的意思。

items.example: Remanere is the direct Latin ancestor.
items.exampleCN: remanere 是直接的拉丁祖先。

items.example: The -s makes the verb into a plural noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 把动词变成复数名词。

items.example: Remnant is a close cousin in meaning.
Permanent keeps the same staying root.
items.exampleCN: permanent 保留同一个「停留」词根。

items.example: Mansion shows the root in a place of dwelling.
items.exampleCN: mansion 展示了这个词根在居住场所上的用法。

definition_zh: 释放；发布；解除；发行物
definition_en: to let a person or a thing go free; to make a film, a record, or a report available to the public; to free someone from a duty or a debt
core_image: 笼门被拉开，一只鸟迟疑了一下才飞出去
scene: 笼门被拉开，里面的鸟迟疑了一下，才振翅飞向树梢。 The government will release the report on Monday.
sceneCN: 这里 release 是「发布」（第 2 个义项：把消息或文件公开给公众）；句意为政府将在周一发布这份报告。画面里可留意：被拉开的笼门、飞向树梢的鸟。

senses.title: To let go free
senses.definition: to stop holding a person or an animal and let it go
senses.definitionCN: 不再抓住某人或某动物，任其离开
senses.example: The keeper released the bird at the edge of the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 管理员在林边放飞了那只鸟。
senses.why: The French word behind it means to let go or give back, so the first sense is simply the opening of a hand or a door.
senses.whyCN: 其背后的法语词意为「放开、交还」，所以第一义就是把手或门打开。

senses.title: To make public
senses.definition: to make a film, a record, or a piece of information available to everyone
senses.definitionCN: 让影片、唱片或信息向所有人公开
senses.example: The government will release the report on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 政府将在周一发布这份报告。
senses.why: A work kept from the public is held tight; making it available is the same letting go, applied to information.
senses.whyCN: 被扣住不公开的作品是攥紧的；让它面世就是同一种「放开」，只是对象变成了信息。

senses.title: To free from an obligation
senses.definition: to free someone from a duty, a debt, or a promise
senses.definitionCN: 使某人免于某项义务、债务或承诺
senses.example: The court released him from the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 法院解除了他在这份合同中的义务。
senses.why: To be bound by a duty is to be held, and to be released is to have that hold removed.
senses.whyCN: 被义务束缚就是被抓住，而被解除就是那只手被移开。

intro.en: Release came into English through a French verb meaning to let go or give back; in English it is a separate word from relax, which was borrowed straight from Latin.
intro.cn: release 经由一个意为「放开、交还」的法语动词进入英语；在英语里它与 relax 是两个词，后者直接借自拉丁语。

items.en: Old French laissier meant to let, leave, or let go, and it stands behind the second half of the word.
items.cn: 古法语 laissier 意为让、留下或放开，构成这个词的后半部分。

items.en: Relesser joined re- with laissier and meant to let go, give back, or remit.
items.cn: relesser 由 re- 与 laissier 组合，意为放开、交还或免除。

items.en: The French noun reles named a letting go, a remission of a debt, or a release from custody.
items.cn: 法语名词 reles 指放开、债务的免除或从拘押中释放。

items.en: English borrowed both the verb and the noun, keeping the senses of freeing and remitting.
items.cn: 英语同时借入动词与名词，保留了「释放」与「免除」两义。

items.en: Publishing gave the word its sense of issuing a film, a record, or a statement to the public.
items.cn: 出版业赋予这个词「向公众发行影片、唱片或声明」的意义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that begin like release; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of freeing and issuing.
note.cn: 形近组收与 release 开头相近的词；近义组收表示释放与发行的动词。

entries.definition: The easing of pain or worry.
entries.definitionCN: 缓解；宽慰。

entries.definition: To pass something on.
entries.definitionCN: 转达；接力。

entries.definition: To enjoy greatly.
entries.definitionCN: 享受；喜爱。

entries.definition: To let someone go.
entries.definitionCN: 释放。

entries.definition: To let a person or a substance go out.
entries.definitionCN: 释放；排出。

entries.definition: To make a work available to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 出版；发布。

entries.definition: To give out officially.
entries.definitionCN: 发布；发放。

normalIntro.en: The word is a letting go: a hand opens, a film reaches the public, a duty falls away.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「松手」：手打开，影片抵达公众，义务随之脱落。

normal.en: Re plus lease, back plus let: to let something go back to freedom.
normal.cn: re 加 lease，往回加让：让某物回到自由。

normal.en: Press release is a sheet handed to journalists.
normal.cn: press release 是发给记者的那张纸。

normal.en: A film release is the day the public may see it.
normal.cn: a film release 是公众可以看到它的日子。

normal.en: Release a prisoner is the plainest use of the word.
normal.cn: release a prisoner 是这个词最朴素的用法。

normal.en: Release and relax are separate words in English; keep them apart.
normal.cn: release 与 relax 在英语里是两个词，要分清。

abstract.en: To release is to admit that holding on has stopped helping.
abstract.cn: 释放，就是承认攥着已经不再有用。

abstract.en: A government releases only what it can no longer hide.
abstract.cn: 政府只发布它再也藏不住的东西。

abstract.en: What is released does not always choose where it goes.
abstract.cn: 被放出的东西，并不总能选择去向。

examples.en: The government will release the report on Monday.
examples.cn: 政府将在周一发布这份报告。

examples.en: The keeper released the bird at the edge of the wood.
examples.cn: 管理员在林边放飞了那只鸟。

examples.en: The court released him from the contract.
examples.cn: 法院解除了他在这份合同中的义务。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回、放开）加 lease（让）：松开手让出去，是释放；把影片或消息让给公众，是发布；把义务让掉，是解除。

root: 古法语 laissier（让、放开）→ relesser（放开、交还、免除）→ 名词 reles → 英语 release；与直接借自拉丁 relaxare 的 relax 是两个分别进入英语的词，不可互训。同族有 releaser、releasable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is letting go; the senses move from opening a cage, to issuing a work to the public, to removing a duty.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「放开」；义项从打开笼子，到向公众发行作品，再到解除一项义务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cage door pulled open and a bird hesitating before it flies.
core.cn: 核心意象：笼门被拉开，一只鸟迟疑了一下才飞出去。

branches.en: a bird leaving its cage
branches.cn: 离开笼子的鸟

branches.en: a report handed to the press
branches.cn: 交给媒体的报告

branches.en: a contract no longer binding
branches.cn: 不再有约束力的合同

branches.en: a body freed and an obligation lifted
branches.cn: 被放开的人与被卸下的义务

branches.en: a statement issued and a debt forgiven
branches.cn: 发布的声明与免除的债务

intro.en: A French verb of letting go enters English with its noun, and the single idea of releasing covers prisoners, films, and debts.
intro.cn: 一个法语表「放开」的动词连同其名词进入英语，而「放开」这一个观念覆盖囚犯、影片与债务。

latinIntro.en: The stem is French, from laissier, to let; the prefix re- means back, so no Latin root is listed for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自法语 laissier（让），前缀 re- 表「往回」，因此本词不列拉丁词根。

definition_zh: 乐意地；容易地；随时可用地
definition_en: willingly and without hesitation; easily and without difficulty; in a way that is available at hand
core_image: 工具摆在手边，一伸手就能拿到
scene: 工具都摆在工作台手边，需要时一伸手就能拿到。 She readily agreed to help.
sceneCN: 这里 readily 是「乐意地」（第 1 个义项：毫不犹豫地愿意）；句意为她欣然同意帮忙。画面里可留意：摆在工作台手边的工具、伸出的手。

pos.zh: 乐意地；容易地；随时可用地

derivatives.zh: readily 去掉 -ly，指准备好的、乐意的
ready 加 -ness，指准备就绪、乐意
ready 与 made 复合，指现成的

senses.title: Willingly
senses.definition: willingly and without hesitation
senses.definitionCN: 愿意且毫不犹豫
senses.example: She readily agreed to help.
senses.exampleCN: 她欣然同意帮忙。
senses.why: Readily is ready with the adverb ending, and ready already meant prepared, so the adverb says the mind is prepared to say yes.
senses.whyCN: readily 是 ready 加副词词尾，而 ready 本就意为「准备好」，因此这个副词说心已准备好答应。

senses.title: Easily
senses.definition: easily, without difficulty or delay
senses.definitionCN: 轻而易举、没有困难或拖延
senses.example: The information is readily understood by beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 初学者也能轻易理解这些信息。
senses.why: What is ready at hand is also easy to use, so the word passed from willingness to ease of doing.
senses.whyCN: 手边现成之物也便于使用，于是这个词从「乐意」转到「容易」。

senses.title: At hand
senses.definition: in a state of being available whenever needed
senses.definitionCN: 处于需要时随时可用的状态
senses.example: Clean water is readily available in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市里干净的水随时可得。
senses.why: The oldest sense of ready is prepared, and what is prepared is already there when wanted, hence readily available.
senses.whyCN: ready 最古老的意思就是「准备好」，准备好的东西在需要时已经在那里，因此有了 readily available。

intro.en: Readily is ready with the adverb ending -ly; ready goes back to Old English ræde, prepared, from rædan, to arrange or advise.
intro.cn: readily 是 ready 加副词词尾 -ly；ready 可追溯到古英语 ræde（准备好的），源自动词 rædan（安排、劝告）。

items.en: Ræde meant prepared or ready, of a person or a thing made fit for use.
items.cn: ræde 意为准备好的，指人或物已被安排得适于使用。

items.en: Middle English kept ready for what is prepared, and extended it to a willing mind.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 ready 表示「准备好的」，并把它扩展到乐意的态度。

items.en: The ending -ly turned ready into readily, meaning in a ready manner.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把 ready 变成 readily，意为以准备好的方式。

items.en: A mind ready to agree is a mind that agrees readily, and a thing ready at hand is one used readily.
items.cn: 准备好同意的心，就是欣然同意的心；手边现成之物，就是容易使用之物。

items.en: Modern English uses readily for willing agreement, for easy understanding, and for what is available at hand.
items.cn: 现代英语用 readily 指乐意的同意、容易的理解，以及手边可得之物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers ready forms and one confusable adverb; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of willingness and ease.
note.cn: 形近组收 ready 的形式与一个易混副词；近义组收表示意愿与容易的副词。

entries.definition: Prepared or willing.
entries.definitionCN: 准备好的或乐意的。

entries.definition: The state of being ready.
entries.definitionCN: 准备好的状态。

entries.definition: Made in advance and available at once.
entries.definitionCN: 预先做好、立即可用的。

entries.definition: Before now, a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 在此前，另一词。

entries.definition: With a willing attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 以愿意的态度。

entries.definition: Without difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 没有困难地。

entries.definition: Quickly and without delay.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速而不拖延地。

entries.definition: Without problems or interruption.
entries.definitionCN: 没有问题或中断地。

normalIntro.en: The adverb draws on ready as prepared: prepared to agree is willing, prepared at hand is easy, prepared in advance is available.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词取 ready「准备好」之意：准备好同意就是乐意，准备好手边就是容易，预先准备好就是随时可用。

normal.en: Readily is ready with -ly, so it says something is done in a ready manner.
normal.cn: readily 是 ready 加 -ly，说明某事以准备好的方式完成。

normal.en: She readily agreed means she was ready to say yes.
normal.cn: She readily agreed 意为她准备好答应。

normal.en: Readily available means the thing is already there when you need it.
normal.cn: readily available 意为需要时东西已经在那里。

normal.en: What is readily understood is understood without effort.
normal.cn: readily understood 之物，理解起来不费力。

normal.en: Ready and already look alike, but already means before now.
normal.cn: ready 与 already 形近，但 already 意为「在此之前」。

abstract.en: Readily measures the distance between a need and an answer.
abstract.cn: readily 衡量的是需求与答案之间的距离。

abstract.en: A thing readily given may still be carefully chosen.
abstract.cn: 乐意给出的东西，也可能是经过仔细选择的。

abstract.en: The easier something is to use, the more readily it is used.
abstract.cn: 某物越容易使用，就越常被使用。

examples.en: She readily agreed to help.
examples.cn: 她欣然同意帮忙。

examples.en: The information is readily understood by beginners.
examples.cn: 初学者也能轻易理解这些信息。

examples.en: Clean water is readily available in the city.
examples.cn: 这座城市里干净的水随时可得。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「工具摆在手边」——伸手就能拿，随时能用，记住 readily 是乐意地、容易地。

root: 古英语 rædan（安排、劝告）→ ræde（准备好的）→ 英语 ready + 副词后缀 -ly → readily；同族有 ready、readiness、ready-made。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being prepared; the senses divide into a willing mind, an easy action, and a thing at hand.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「已准备好」；义项分为乐意的心、容易的动作，以及手边可得之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tools laid out within reach on a workbench, ready for the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：工具摆在手边的工作台上，等着手去拿。

branches.en: a ready yes before the question ends
branches.cn: 问题未完就答应的 yes

branches.en: a task finished without effort
branches.cn: 不费力就完成的任务

branches.en: clean water waiting in a tap
branches.cn: 水龙头里随时可得的净水

branches.en: willing hands and easy work
branches.cn: 乐意的手与容易的活

branches.en: easy to use and there when needed
branches.cn: 易于使用且需要时就在

intro.en: The word is ready plus the adverb ending -ly, built on a native adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词是 ready 加副词词尾 -ly，建立在一条本族形容词上。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 测量；量出；尺寸；措施；分寸；程度；节拍；格律
definition_en: to find the size or amount of something; a step taken to deal with a problem; a standard or a degree of something
core_image: 一把卷尺贴住桌沿，读出的数字被写进料单，旁边压着一张应对步骤的便签
scene: 木工把卷尺贴住桌沿，读出长度，再把数字写在料单上。 Carpenters measure every board twice before the saw is switched on.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：测定某物的尺寸或数量；句意为木工在开锯之前把每块板量两遍。图中可辨识物件：卷尺、桌沿、料单、铅笔；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 尺寸；量度；措施；分寸；（音乐的）小节；格律

senses.title: To find a size or amount
senses.definition: to find the size, length, weight or amount of something by using a tool or a standard
senses.definitionCN: 用工具或标准求出某物的尺寸、长度、重量或数量
senses.example: Carpenters measure every board twice before the saw is switched on.
senses.exampleCN: 木工在开锯之前把每块板量两遍。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to measure, and the physical act of comparing against a standard is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词本意就是测量，拿某物与标准相比较的实体动作是最古老的一层。

senses.title: The number obtained
senses.definition: the size or amount that a measurement produces, often written as a figure with a unit
senses.definitionCN: 测量得出的尺寸或数量，常写成带单位的数字
senses.example: The measure came out at two metres, not one.
senses.exampleCN: 量出来的结果是一点九米，不是一米。
senses.why: A measurement is both the act and its outcome, so the noun carries the number as well as the procedure.
senses.whyCN: 测量既是动作也是结果，因此这个名词既携带数字，也携带过程。

senses.title: A step taken to fix something
senses.titleCN: 为解决问题所采取的步骤
senses.definition: an action or policy adopted to deal with a problem or to reach an aim
senses.definitionCN: 为处理问题或达到目的而采取的行动或政策
senses.example: The city took measures to cut traffic at the school gate.
senses.exampleCN: 市里采取措施减少校门口的交通。
senses.why: A step is a measured amount of action: enough to change the situation, not more, and the metaphor runs from dose to policy.
senses.whyCN: 一个步骤就是定量的行动：足以改变局面，又不过量，这个比喻从剂量一直走到政策。

senses.title: A proposed law
senses.definition: in a legislature, a proposed law put forward for debate and vote
senses.definitionCN: 在立法机构中提交辩论与表决的法律草案
senses.example: The measure passed by three votes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案以三票之差通过。
senses.why: A bill is a measured response written into legal form, and American usage kept the word for the draft itself.
senses.whyCN: 法案是把有分寸的应对写成法律形式，美式用法保留了这个词来指草案本身。

senses.title: A standard for comparison
senses.definition: a standard, unit or benchmark by which other things are judged
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断其他事物的标准、单位或基准
senses.example: Test scores are a crude measure of a school.
senses.exampleCN: 考试分数是对学校的一种粗略衡量。
senses.why: To measure anything one needs a fixed unit, and the noun then names any yardstick, including an abstract one.
senses.whyCN: 要测量任何东西都需要固定单位，名词随后指任何标尺，包括抽象的标尺。

senses.title: A degree or extent
senses.definition: the extent to which something is true or present, as in in large measure
senses.definitionCN: 某事物为真或存在的程度，如「在很大程度上」
senses.example: The success was in large measure due to the technicians.
senses.exampleCN: 这次成功在很大程度上要归功于技术人员。
senses.why: An amount can be spoken of without a ruler, so the word extends from physical quantity to degree of influence.
senses.whyCN: 数量可以不用尺子来说，于是这个词从物理量扩展到影响的程度。

senses.title: A limit or moderation
senses.definition: a proper limit in behaviour or feeling, or the absence of one in beyond measure
senses.definitionCN: 行为或情感上应有的限度，或在「无法估量」中表示没有限度
senses.example: His anger went beyond measure.
senses.exampleCN: 他的愤怒到了无法估量的地步。
senses.why: The idea of a fixed amount turns moral: to keep measure is to keep within bounds, and to exceed it is to lose proportion.
senses.whyCN: 固定数量的观念转向道德：守分寸就是守在界限内，越过就是失去比例。

senses.title: A bar in music
senses.definition: a group of beats between two bar lines, the unit of musical time
senses.definitionCN: 两条小节线之间的一组拍子，是音乐时间的基本单位
senses.example: The phrase fits one measure of four beats.
senses.exampleCN: 这个乐句正好占一小节四拍。
senses.why: Music divides time into equal measured spans, so the word for measuring became the name of the span.
senses.whyCN: 音乐把时间分成等长的段，于是表示测量的词成了那一段的名字。

senses.title: The metre of a line
senses.definition: the patterned rhythm of a line of verse, counted in feet
senses.definitionCN: 诗句中有规律的节奏，以音步计数
senses.example: The poem keeps a steady measure through twelve lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗十二行都保持稳定的格律。
senses.why: Verse counts syllables the way a ruler counts inches, and the noun for the count became the name of the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 诗句像尺子量英寸那样数音节，表示计数的名词就成了这种模式的名字。

intro.en: Measure comes from Old French mesure, from Latin mensura 'a measuring', built on metiri 'to measure'. The root is generally connected with a very old word for measure that also gave Greek metron and English metre.
intro.cn: measure 来自古法语 mesure，源头是拉丁语 mensura「测量」，由 metiri「测量」构成。这个词根一般认为与一个极古老的「度量」词相关，希腊语 metron 与英语 metre 也出自它。

items.en: Metiri meant to measure or apportion, and it is the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: metiri 意为测量、按量分配，是整个词族背后的动词。

items.en: Mensura named the act and the result of measuring, and it passed through French as the English noun.
items.cn: mensura 指测量的动作与结果，经法语成为英语名词。

items.en: The old root is generally reconstructed as a word for measure, the same one behind metre and metric; the reconstruction is accepted but the exact shape is source uncertain.
items.cn: 这个古老词根一般被重构为表示「度量」的词，metre 与 metric 也出自它；这一重构被接受，但确切形态来源不确定。

items.en: Old French mesure carried both the physical and the moral senses, and English took the pair together in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 mesure 同时带有物理与道德两层意思，英语在十三世纪把两者一起接收。

items.en: American usage of the eighteenth century applied measure to a proposed law, a use that British English largely dropped.
items.cn: 十八世纪的美式用法把这个词用到法律草案上，英式英语后来大体放弃了这一用法。

items.en: Latin mensura had already named the counted span in rhythm, and English kept measure for a bar and for metrical pattern.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mensura 早已用来指节奏中被数出的段落，英语保留 measure 指小节与格律。

note.en: The first group shares the measuring root; the second group names related actions or quantities.
note.cn: 第一组共享「测量」词根；第二组是相关动作或数量。

entries.definition: The act or the figure produced by measuring.
entries.definitionCN: 测量的动作，或测量得出的数字。

entries.definition: Large or stable enough to be measured.
entries.definitionCN: 大到或稳定到可以被测量的。

entries.definition: Deliberate and restrained, as if each step were weighed.
entries.definitionCN: 审慎而有节制的，仿佛每一步都称过。

entries.definition: The process, or a compound for a tool such as a measuring tape.
entries.definitionCN: 测量过程，或构成卷尺一类工具名。

entries.definition: The mathematics of lengths, areas and volumes; a learned doublet.
entries.definitionCN: 研究长度、面积与体积的数学；学术性的同源词。

entries.definition: To estimate or measure, often with an instrument; also the instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 估计或测量，常借助仪器；也指该仪器。

entries.definition: To express something as a number.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物表示为数字。

entries.definition: To judge the value or level of something, with less emphasis on units.
entries.definitionCN: 判断某物的价值或水平，对单位的强调较少。

entries.definition: An action taken toward a goal, the everyday word behind the policy sense.
entries.definitionCN: 为达到目标而采取的行动，是政策义背后的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin measuring verb, the real family and the fixed phrases of policy and tools.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语测量动词、真实同族词，以及政策与工具里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin metiri meant to measure, and mensura gave English the noun through French.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 metiri 意为测量，mensura 经法语给了英语这个名词。

normal.en: The family runs measure, measurement, measurable, measured and measuring.
normal.cn: 同族词有 measure、measurement、measurable、measured 与 measuring。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: take measures, safety measures, in large measure, beyond measure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：采取措施、安全措施、在很大程度上、无法估量地。

normal.en: A tape measure is the tool, and a measure of success is the standard: one word, two kinds of ruler.
normal.cn: 卷尺是工具，衡量成功的标准是标尺：同一个词，两种尺。

normal.en: Music counts beats into a measure, and verse counts feet into a measure.
normal.cn: 音乐把拍子数成小节，诗句把音步数成格律。

abstract.en: To keep measure is to know how much is enough, which is a moral skill before it is a mathematical one.
abstract.cn: 守分寸就是知道多少算够，这先是道德的技能，然后才是数学的。

abstract.en: What can be measured is not always what matters, and what matters is not always measurable.
abstract.cn: 可测量的不总是重要的，重要的也不总是可测量的。

abstract.en: A measure is a decision about what counts, made before any number appears.
abstract.cn: 尺度是在数字出现之前，关于「什么算数」的决定。

examples.en: The nurse measured the wound and wrote the figure in the chart.
examples.cn: 护士量了伤口的大小，把数字写进病历。

examples.en: The council adopted three measures to reduce waste.
examples.cn: 议会通过三项措施减少浪费。

examples.en: Her patience was tested beyond measure that afternoon.
examples.cn: 那天下午，她的耐心受到了无法估量的考验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「米热」——用尺子一点点比过去，看看到底有多长：测量

root: 拉丁语 metiri「测量」→ mensura「测量、量度」→ 古法语 mesure → 英语 measure。词根一般认为与古希腊语 metron 同源，确切形态属重构，来源不确定；法案、小节与格律义均为后起扩展。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one ruler: the act of measuring, the number it gives, a policy step, a bill, a standard, a degree of influence, a moral limit, a musical bar and a line's metre.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一把尺：测量的动作、量出的数字、政策步骤、法案、比较标准、影响程度、道德限度、音乐小节与诗句格律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tape is laid along the desk, and the number goes straight onto the cutting list.
core.cn: 核心意象：卷尺贴住桌沿，数字直接写进下料单。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE FIGURE: laying a tape down, and the number that comes back.
branches.cn: 动作与数字：把尺子贴上去，以及报回来的那个数。

branches.en: THE POLICY DOSE: a step sized to the problem, and the same step written as a bill.
branches.cn: 政策剂量：按问题大小配出的步骤，以及写成法案的同一步骤。

branches.en: THE YARDSTICK: test scores used as a crude ruler for a school.
branches.cn: 标尺：把考试分数当作衡量学校的粗尺。

branches.en: THE DEGREE AND THE LIMIT: influence measured in large part, anger that passes all bounds.
branches.cn: 程度与限度：占很大部分的影响，与越过一切界限的愤怒。

branches.en: THE COUNTED SPAN: four beats between two bar lines, feet counted through a line of verse.
branches.cn: 被数出的段落：两条小节线之间的四拍，与一行诗里数出的音步。

intro.en: Measure is a Latin noun and verb of measuring, and the family keeps both the physical tool and the abstract standard.
intro.cn: measure 是拉丁语中表示测量的名词与动词，其词族同时保留实体工具与抽象标准两面。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is metiri, mensura and the adjective mensurabilis, with French mesure as the carrier into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 metiri、mensura 与形容词 mensurabilis，古法语 mesure 则是进入英语的载体。

items.example: The noun carries both the act and the standard.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时携带动作与标准。

items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的根。

items.example: It named both the act and its result.
It builds nouns of outcome, as in mensura.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示结果的词，如 mensura。

items.example: French added the moral sense of keeping within bounds.
items.exampleCN: 法语加上了守界限的道德含义。

items.meaning: the act or result of measuring
items.example: The English suffix names the process.
The participle turned the noun into a manner.
items.exampleCN: 分词把名词变成了举止。

items.example: The negative suffix marks what cannot be counted.
items.exampleCN: 否定词尾标出无法计数之物。

items.example: The learned doublet stays close to Latin.
items.exampleCN: 这个学术同源词紧贴拉丁语。

latinEntries.structure: Latin deponent verb metiri (met-, mensus; to measure)
latinEntries.example: Latin metiri means to measure or allot.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 metiri 意为测量、分配。

latinEntries.example: Latin mensura means a measuring, and gives English measure.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 mensura 意为测量，并给出英语 measure。

latinEntries.structure: Latin noun suffix -ura (result of an action)
latinEntries.example: Latin -ura builds nouns such as cultura, cultivation.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -ura 构成 cultura（耕作）这类名词。
拉丁语 mensurabilis 意为可测量的。

definition_zh: 打算；想要；意为
definition_en: to have a plan or purpose in mind, or to be meant for a particular use
core_image: 弓弦被拉紧，箭尖指向远处的一点，手还没松开
scene: 院子里搭了一半的木架，工具摆在地上，主人正看着图纸。 We intend to finish the fence before the first frost.
sceneCN: 这里 intend 是「打算」（第 1 个义项：心里已有计划），句意为我们打算在第一场霜前把篱笆修完。画面里的物件：半成品木架、工具、图纸。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「意图；打算」
由同一词干构成，义为「意图」；也作形容词「专注的」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「预期的；预定的」
由否定前缀 un- 加过去分词构成，义为「非故意的」

senses.title: Plan to do something
senses.definition: to have something in mind as a plan or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把某事件作为计划或目的放在心上
senses.example: They intend to move the shop closer to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们打算把店搬到离车站更近的地方。
senses.why: Latin intendere means to stretch towards, like a bow aimed at a mark.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 intendere 意为「朝……伸展」，像弓瞄准靶子。

senses.title: Mean something by words
senses.definition: to mean a particular thing by what one says or does
senses.definitionCN: 指通过言语或行为想表达某个特定的意思
senses.example: I intended a warning, not a joke.
senses.exampleCN: 我想表达的是警告，不是玩笑。
senses.why: Mind is a kind of aim: words are arrows shot at a hearer's understanding.
senses.whyCN: 心意也是一种瞄准：话是射向听者理解的箭。

senses.title: Be meant for a use
senses.definition: to be planned or designed for a particular person or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某个人或某种目的而规划或设计
senses.example: The small room was intended for the children.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小房间是为孩子们准备的。
senses.why: The passive form focuses on the target of the aim rather than on the planner.
senses.whyCN: 被动形式把注意力从计划者移到被瞄准的用途上。

intro.en: Intend comes from Latin intendere "to stretch towards", the same verb that gives tension and attention.
intro.cn: intend 来自拉丁语 intendere「朝……伸展」，与 tension、attention 同一动词。

items.en: Tendere "to stretch" joined in- "towards" to make intendere.
items.cn: tendere「伸展」与 in-「朝向」合成 intendere。

items.en: Archers used intendere arcum, to bend a bow, always aiming at something.
items.cn: 弓箭手用 intendere arcum 表示「弯弓」，总是指向某物。

items.en: The noun intentio named the act of aiming the mind.
items.cn: 名词 intentio 指让心瞄准的动作。

items.en: French entendre "to mean, to understand" carried the word into English.
items.cn: 法语 entendre（意为、听懂）把这个词带入英语。

items.en: English fixed the spelling intend and the contrast with intend versus attend.
items.cn: 英语固定了拼写 intend，并与 attend 形成对照。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tendere root of stretching; the near-meaning group holds other words for planning.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「伸展」的词根 tendere；近义组收其他表示计划的词。

entries.definition: The noun for purpose; the adjective for being focused.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「意图」，形容词义为「专注的」。

entries.definition: To stretch something out or forward.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「伸展；延长」。

entries.definition: To stretch the mind towards a meeting or a task.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「出席」，原指把心伸向某事。

entries.definition: To arrange the steps of a future action.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「计划」，安排未来行动的步骤。

entries.definition: To have something as one's purpose by nature.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「意欲」，侧重语言本身所指。

entries.definition: To point at a target, literally or figuratively.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「瞄准；旨在」，字面或比喻皆可。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the stretched bow inside the word and its habitual phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用词里那张拉开的弓以及它的习惯搭配。

normal.en: in plus tend: stretch the mind towards a target.
normal.cn: in 加 tend：把心思朝靶子伸过去。

normal.en: We intend to finish early, and as intended we do.
normal.cn: 我们打算早点完成，也如预期完成了。

normal.en: The knife is intended for bread, not for wood.
normal.cn: 这把刀是为切面包准备的，不是砍木头的。

normal.en: Intend has a plan; attention has a focus.
normal.cn: intend 是有计划，attention 是有焦点。

normal.en: He intended no harm, only a quiet warning.
normal.cn: 他并无恶意，只是想轻声警告。

abstract.en: To intend is to draw a bow before saying a word.
abstract.cn: 打算就是在开口前先把弓拉开。

abstract.en: An intention is an arrow released only half way.
abstract.cn: 意图是一支只射出一半的箭。

abstract.en: People judge the deed, while you remember the aim.
abstract.cn: 别人评判行为，你自己记得当初的瞄准。

examples.en: We intend to keep the old sign over the door.
examples.cn: 我们打算把门上那块旧招牌留着。

examples.en: She intended her remark as a warning, not an insult.
examples.cn: 她那句话是想提醒，而不是侮辱。

examples.en: The path was intended for walkers, not bicycles.
examples.cn: 这条小路是为步行者修的，不是给自行车的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因疼的」——还没动手就先因想着而心疼，那是打算

root: 拉丁语 tendere「伸展」→ in-「朝向」+ tendere → intendere「朝……伸展、瞄准」→ 古法语 entendre → 英语 intend。同族词：intention、intent、extend、attend。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: planning to act, meaning a certain thing, and being designed for a purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：计划去做、话里想要表达，以及为某用途而设定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drawn bow aimed at a distant mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张拉满的弓指向远处的靶点。

branches.en: THE PLAN: the bow is drawn for tomorrow's task.
branches.cn: 计划这条线：为明天的任务拉开的弓。

branches.en: THE REMARK: words are aimed at a hearer's mind.
branches.cn: 话语这条线：话瞄准听者的头脑。

branches.en: THE SMALL ROOM: a space is aimed at one kind of user.
branches.cn: 小房间这条线：空间瞄准某一类使用者。

branches.en: THE LINK: both are aims inside a mind.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都是心里的瞄准。

branches.en: THE LINK: what is planned is also what is designed.
branches.cn: 连接线：所打算的也正是所设计的。

intro.en: Intend = in- "towards" + the root tend- "stretch", with no separate English suffix.
intro.cn: intend = in-「朝向」+ 词根 tend-「伸展」，没有单独的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere, intendere and intentio are all attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tendere、intendere、intentio 均有记载。

items.exampleCN: 也见于 tension 与 tendon。

items.example: The verb alone means to stretch out.
It is the noun behind intention.
items.exampleCN: 它是 intention 背后的名词。

definition_zh: 陡峭的；陡直的；（价格等）过高的；浸泡；浸渍
definition_en: rising or falling quickly over a short distance, or to leave something in liquid to soak
core_image: 一面几乎垂直的岩壁立在山路上——向上看去帽子都会掉
scene: 徒步到半山，向导指着前方的岩壁示意大家抓稳。 The path became so steep that we had to use ropes near the top.
sceneCN: 这里 steep 是形容词「陡峭的」（第 1 个义项：短时间内急速升降）；句意为接近山顶时坡度陡得我们不得不借助绳索。

pos.zh: 形容词：陡峭的；（价格）过高的

collocations.phrase: steep the tea for five minutes

collocations.zh: 浸透着历史；富有历史底蕴

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「陡峭地；急剧地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「陡峭程度」

senses.title: Rising or falling quickly over a short distance
senses.definition: sloping sharply upward or downward, hard to climb or walk
senses.definitionCN: 坡度急剧向上或向下，难以攀爬或行走
senses.example: They climbed the steep slope with both hands on the rocks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们双手抓着岩石攀上陡坡。
senses.why: The wall-like slope that forces your body almost flat against it.
senses.whyCN: 近乎墙壁的斜坡逼得人身体几乎贴上去。

senses.title: Too high, especially of prices or demands
senses.definition: unreasonably high, as an amount of money or a demand
senses.definitionCN: 指金额或要求高得不合理
senses.example: Two hundred yuan for a bowl of noodles is a bit steep.
senses.exampleCN: 一碗面两百块有点贵得离谱。
senses.why: The price climbs as suddenly as the rock wall.
senses.whyCN: 价格像岩壁一样陡然爬升，令人望而生畏。

senses.title: To leave something in liquid to soak
senses.definition: to keep food, leaves, or other material in liquid so flavor or substance is drawn out
senses.definitionCN: 把食物、茶叶等泡在液体中使味道或成分释出
senses.example: Steep the dried mushrooms in warm water for half an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 把干香菇在温水里泡半小时。
senses.why: The leaf sinks down a steep drop into the water and stays.
senses.whyCN: 叶子陡然沉入水底并停留其中，即浸泡。

senses.title: Deeply filled with or influenced by something
senses.definition: deeply involved in or shaped by something, as steeped in tradition
senses.definitionCN: 深受某事物浸润或影响，如 steeped in tradition
senses.example: The old quarter is steeped in history and legend.
senses.exampleCN: 老城区浸透着历史与传说。
senses.why: Soaked so long in the liquid of tradition that its color fills everything.
senses.whyCN: 在传统的汁液中泡得足够久，颜色浸透了每个角落。

intro.en: The steep of slopes and the steep of soaking are two ancient roots that happen to share a spelling.
intro.cn: 「陡峭」的 steep 与「浸泡」的 steep 是两个恰好同形的古老词根。

items.en: One reconstructed root *staipa- is thought to mean steep or sharp; another *staup- meant to push under liquid.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *staipa- 意为陡、尖；另一词根 *staup- 意为按入液体。

items.en: Steep meant high and sharp-sloped; steap (verb) meant to dip into liquid.
items.cn: 古英语 steep 指高耸陡斜；动词 steap 指浸入液体。

items.en: Both words kept their forms and senses side by side.
items.cn: 中古英语中两个词形义并存，并行发展。

items.en: The price sense grew as a metaphor of the sharp climb; steeped in took the soaking image into character.
items.cn: 价格义由「陡升」比喻而来；steeped in 把浸泡意象带入品格。

items.en: Tea-making fixed the everyday verb, while steep prices and steep learning curves stayed common.
items.cn: 泡茶固定了日常动词用法，steep prices 与 steep learning curves 仍是常用表达。

note.en: Steep looks like the unrelated step, and sits near slope words and soak words of different roots.
note.cn: steep 拼写上与不相关的 step 相近，义场靠近词源不同的坡度词与浸泡词。

entries.definition: a single movement of one foot, or a stage in a process
entries.definitionCN: 脚步；步骤；与 steep 只差一个字母，词源不同

entries.definition: a farm animal kept for wool and meat
entries.definitionCN: 绵羊；拼读相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a tall pointed tower on a church
entries.definitionCN: 教堂尖塔；与 steep 同根，指高耸陡直之物

entries.definition: almost completely vertical, as a cliff
entries.definitionCN: 近乎垂直的；陡峭的，比 steep 更强调垂直

entries.definition: sudden and large, as a rise or fall
entries.definitionCN: 急剧的；猛烈的，强调变化的突然

entries.definition: to leave something in liquid until it is wet through
entries.definitionCN: 浸泡；浸湿，与 steep 的动词义相近

entries.definition: not steep or sudden, as a slope
entries.definitionCN: 平缓的；缓和的，与陡峭相反

normalIntro.en: Keep steep apart from step, and link the slope to the price and the teapot.
normalIntro.cn: 区分 steep 与 step，把坡度、价格与茶壶三个画面串联起来。

normal.en: Steep and step differ by one letter: the wall or the stair.
normal.cn: steep 与 step 只差一个字母：一面墙或一级台阶。

normal.en: A steep price climbs as sharply as a steep hill.
normal.cn: steep price 与 steep hill 共享「陡然爬升」意象。

normal.en: Steep the tea is the kitchen verb for soaking leaves.
normal.cn: steep the tea 是泡茶叶的日常动词说法。

normal.en: Steeped in history keeps the soaking image for culture.
normal.cn: steeped in history 把浸泡意象用于文化底蕴。

normal.en: A steep learning curve warns that progress will be hard at first.
normal.cn: steep learning curve 警示入门阶段难度很大。

abstract.en: Tilt your head back to see the rock wall rise above the path.
abstract.cn: 仰头看岩壁在小径上方高高竖起。

abstract.en: Watch the price line on a chart jump almost vertically.
abstract.cn: 看图表上的价格线几乎垂直跳升。

abstract.en: See tea leaves slowly sink and unfurl in hot water.
abstract.cn: 看茶叶在热水中缓缓下沉舒展。

examples.en: The hill was too steep for the old truck to climb.
examples.cn: 山坡太陡，旧卡车爬不上去。

examples.en: The fee seemed steep, so we compared other schools.
examples.cn: 这笔费用显得过高，于是我们对比了其他学校。

examples.en: Let the herbs steep in the oil overnight.
examples.cn: 让香草在油里浸泡一夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯提普」——谐音「死梯坡」：这段梯子一样的坡死陡死陡，爬上去要命。

root: 「陡峭」义源自日耳曼语 *staipa-（陡、尖，一般认为存疑）；「浸泡」义源自另一日耳曼词根 *staup-（按入液体）；二者同形异源，均经古英语进入现代英语。

sensesIntro.en: The vertical wall gives the sharp slope, the climbing price, and the drop into water where leaves soak and minds steep in tradition.
sensesIntro.cn: 垂直的岩壁给出急坡、陡涨的价格，以及叶子沉入水中浸泡、心灵浸透传统的画面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall-like slope rising faster than your legs can manage
core.cn: 核心意象：一面腿脚跟不上、近乎墙壁的斜坡

branches.en: the physical sharp slope
branches.cn: 实体的陡坡

branches.en: the price that climbs like the slope
branches.cn: 像陡坡一样爬升的价格

branches.en: the leaf dropping into liquid to soak
branches.cn: 叶子沉入液体中浸泡

branches.en: a mind soaked full of tradition
branches.cn: 被传统浸透的心灵

branches.en: sharp upward change in ground or in cost
branches.cn: 地面与价格上同样陡急的变化

intro.en: Steep forms few derivatives, but its compounds show both ancient roots at work.
intro.cn: steep 的派生词不多，但复合词显示出两个古老词根的用武之地。

latinIntro.en: Steep has no Latin relatives; both roots are native Germanic, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: steep 没有拉丁同源词，两个词根均为日耳曼本土来源，故拉丁同族词列表为空。

items.meaningCN: 脚步；步骤（与 steep 无关）

items.meaning: to leave in liquid until wet

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「陡峭地；急剧地」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「陡峭程度」

definition_zh: 解决办法；溶液；解答
definition_en: a way to deal with a problem, a liquid with something dissolved in it, or an answer to a puzzle
core_image: 一只手把缠住的绳结慢慢解开
scene: 团队找到了一个简单的解决办法。 The team found a simple solution.
sceneCN: 这里 solution 是「解决办法」（第 1 个义项）；句意：团队找到了一个简单的解决办法。

senses.title: Way to solve
senses.definition: a way of dealing with a problem or difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 处理问题或困难的方法
senses.example: The team found a simple solution.
senses.exampleCN: 团队找到了一个简单的解决办法。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的现代义项。

senses.title: Liquid mixture
senses.definition: a liquid in which another substance has been dissolved
senses.definitionCN: 另一种物质溶解在其中的液体
senses.example: The nurse cleaned the cut with a salt solution.
senses.exampleCN: 护士用盐溶液清洗伤口。
senses.why: Chemistry keeps the older sense of a loosened mixture.
senses.whyCN: 化学保留了混合物被解开的较早含义。

senses.title: Answer to a puzzle
senses.definition: the answer to a puzzle, question, or mathematical problem
senses.definitionCN: 谜题、问题或数学题的答案
senses.example: She checked her solution against the answer key.
senses.exampleCN: 她对照答案检查了自己的解答。
senses.why: A problem is mentally untied.
senses.whyCN: 问题在头脑中被解开。

intro.en: Solution comes from Latin solutio, a loosening.
intro.cn: solution 来自拉丁语 solutio，意为松开。

items.en: Solvere meant to loosen, untie, or pay.
items.cn: solvere 意为松开、解开或支付。

items.en: Solutio meant a loosening or an explanation.
items.cn: solutio 意为松开或解释。

items.en: Solution kept the sense of untangling.
items.cn: solution 保留了理清纠缠的意思。

items.en: The word entered English as solution.
items.cn: 这个词以 solution 进入英语。

items.en: Science gave it the sense of a dissolved mixture.
items.cn: 科学赋予它溶解混合物的意思。

note.en: Solution is compared with look-alike words and words for answers and mixtures.
note.cn: 把 solution 与形近词以及表示答案和混合物的词作比较。

entries.definition: hard and keeping shape
entries.definitionCN: 固体的

entries.definition: the state of being alone
entries.definitionCN: 独处

entries.definition: formal forgiveness of a wrong
entries.definitionCN: 赦免

entries.definition: a reply or a correct response
entries.definitionCN: 答案

entries.definition: a way to cure or fix a problem
entries.definitionCN: 补救办法

entries.definition: a combination of substances
entries.definitionCN: 混合物

normalIntro.en: A solution is a knot that has been loosened.
normalIntro.cn: solution 是一个被解开的结。

normal.en: The team found a simple solution.
normal.cn: 团队找到了一个简单的解决办法。

normal.en: The nurse cleaned the cut with a salt solution.
normal.cn: 护士用盐溶液清洗伤口。

normal.en: She checked her solution against the answer key.
normal.cn: 她对照答案检查了自己的解答。

normal.en: There is no easy solution to the housing problem.
normal.cn: 住房问题没有简单的解决办法。

normal.en: The solution turned the water blue.
normal.cn: 这种溶液把水变成了蓝色。

abstract.en: Every problem looks simpler once it is untied.
abstract.cn: 每个问题一旦被解开，看起来都简单些。

abstract.en: Some answers dissolve rather than break.
abstract.cn: 有些答案是被溶解的，而不是被击碎的。

abstract.en: The word for solving and the word for dissolving are one.
abstract.cn: 解决与溶解在同一个词里。

examples.en: The team found a simple solution.
examples.cn: 团队找到了一个简单的解决办法。

examples.en: The nurse cleaned the cut with a salt solution.
examples.cn: 护士用盐溶液清洗伤口。

examples.en: She checked her solution against the answer key.
examples.cn: 她对照答案检查了自己的解答。

dict_mnemonic.text: solution 与 solve、soluble 同根；find a solution 是「找到解决办法」，salt solution 是「盐溶液」。

root: 拉丁语 solutio（松开、解开），源于 solvere（松开、解开），核心义「把缠结解开」。

sensesIntro.en: Solution is a way to solve a problem, a dissolved liquid mixture, or an answer to a puzzle.
sensesIntro.cn: solution 指解决问题的办法、溶解形成的液体混合物，或谜题的解答。

core.en: A knot loosened until it opens.
core.cn: 被松开到解开的结。

branches.en: A team unties a practical problem.
branches.cn: 团队解开一个实际问题。

branches.en: Salt loosens into water.
branches.cn: 盐在水中化开。

branches.en: A puzzle gives way to an answer.
branches.cn: 谜题让位于答案。

branches.en: Practical and mental problems are both untied.
branches.cn: 实际问题和头脑问题都会被解开。

branches.en: Solving and dissolving share one image of loosening.
branches.cn: 解决与溶解共用「松开」的意象。

intro.en: Solution builds words for solving, dissolving, and answers.
intro.cn: solution 构成表示解决、溶解和答案的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb solvere meant to loosen or untie.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 solvere 意为松开或解开。

items.meaning: a way to solve or a dissolved mixture
items.example: The solution was cheaper than expected.
items.exampleCN: 这个解决办法比预想的便宜。
他们比较了三个解决办法。

items.meaning: to find an answer to a problem
the substance dissolved in a liquid
items.example: The solute settles at the bottom.

items.meaning: to discover a way to fix a problem
items.example: They worked all night to find a solution.
items.exampleCN: 他们通宵工作以找到解决办法。

items.meaning: water with salt dissolved in it
items.example: The salt solution cleans the wound.

items.exampleCN: 他们采取聚焦解决方案的做法。

latinEntries.example: Solvere is the Latin verb behind solution.
latinEntries.exampleCN: solvere 是 solution 背后的拉丁语动词。

definition_zh: 通道；入口；使用权；接触机会；进入；接入；访问；存取
definition_en: a way of entering a place, the right to use or reach something, or the act of reaching or opening it
core_image: 一扇只配了一把钥匙的侧门：能不能进去，全看钥匙在不在你手里
scene: 老小区的正门封了，住户每天都要绕到后街。 The only access to the garden is through a narrow gate.
sceneCN: 这里 access 指「进入的通道」（第 1 个义项：可以进入某处的路径或门）；句意为通往花园的唯一通道是一扇窄门。

pos.zh: 名词：通道；使用权；接触机会；接入
动词：进入；接近；访问；存取

collocations.zh: 通往……的通道；使用……的机会

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -ible 构成，义为「可到达的；可使用的；易懂的」
由 accessible 加后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可达性；无障碍程度」
由否定前缀 in- 加 accessible 构成，义为「难以到达的；难以理解的」
由同一拉丁词根加后缀 -ion 构成，义为「就职；加入；新增」

senses.title: A way in or through
senses.definition: a path, door, road, or other route by which a place can be entered or reached
senses.definitionCN: 指进入或抵达某处的路径、门、道路等
senses.example: The only access to the village is by boat.
senses.exampleCN: 进入这个村子唯一的通道是坐船。
senses.why: Latin accessus was a coming near; a way in is the route that lets that approach happen.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessus 意为「走近」；通道就是让这种走近得以发生的路线。

senses.title: The right to use or obtain
senses.definition: the right or opportunity to use, see, or obtain something that is limited or controlled
senses.definitionCN: 指使用、查看或取得受限事物的权利或机会
senses.example: Every student has access to the online library.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学生都能使用在线图书馆。
senses.why: If a route is open to you, you may walk along it; the route quietly turns into a permission.
senses.whyCN: 如果一条路对你敞开，你就可以沿着它走过去；路线于是悄悄变成了许可。

senses.title: The act of getting in
senses.definition: the act of entering a place or of reaching a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 指进入某地或接触到某人、某物的行为
senses.example: Reporters were refused access to the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 记者被拒绝进入会场。
senses.why: The noun shifts from the route to the movement along it: the approach itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词从「路线」转到「沿路线移动」：也就是走近这个动作本身。

senses.title: A connection to a system
senses.definition: the ability of a device or user to connect to the internet, a network, or a service
senses.definitionCN: 指设备或用户连接互联网、网络或服务的能力
senses.example: The hotel offers free internet access in every room.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆每个房间都提供免费网络接入。
senses.why: A network is treated like a building: you need a way in before you can use what is inside.
senses.whyCN: 网络被当作一栋建筑：先有进去的路，才能使用里面的东西。

senses.title: To reach or enter
senses.definition: to reach, enter, or make use of a place, especially one that is restricted
senses.definitionCN: 指进入、抵达或使用某地，尤指受限之处
senses.example: Staff can access the lab with their ID cards.
senses.exampleCN: 工作人员可以用工牌进入实验室。
senses.why: The verb turns the route into motion: walking the way in.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「路线」变成动作：沿着进去的路走。

senses.title: To open stored data
senses.definition: to open, read, or retrieve files or data stored in a computer system
senses.definitionCN: 指打开、读取或调取计算机系统中存储的文件或数据
senses.example: You can access your files from any device.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以从任何设备访问自己的文件。
senses.why: Data is stored behind a system, and reaching it follows the same pattern as reaching a room.
senses.whyCN: 数据存放在系统之后，取到它的方式和走进一个房间是同一种模式。

senses.title: A sudden fit of feeling
senses.definition: a sudden outburst of an emotion, an old and mostly literary use
senses.definitionCN: 指情绪的突然爆发，属古老且多用于文学的用法
senses.example: In an access of rage, he tore the letter in two.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵暴怒之下，他把信撕成两半。
senses.why: Latin accessus also meant an onset, as if a feeling came upon a person and entered him.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessus 也有「来袭、发作」之意，仿佛一种情绪扑上来，进入了人。

senses.title: Used before a noun for a route
senses.definition: placed before another noun to name a road, code, or point that gives entry
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词之前，表示提供进入的道路、密码或地点
senses.example: Turn left at the access road behind the station.
senses.exampleCN: 在车站后面的辅路向左转。
